supported: Across all three stable-roster Palmer islands, effective colony number declined more rapidly than expected from a time-invariant within-island composition subjected to the observed island-total trajectory and the frozen independent count-error family.
The result survives the inherited uncalibrated Gamma-Poisson CV20% sensitivity in each island individually and jointly.

Adelie population decline in these islands is accompanied by progressive concentration of breeders among a smaller effective set of colony-code breeding components rather than simple proportional thinning.
not_supported: one-to-one physical interpretation of colony codes as mapped subcolony polygons
a causal claim that snow, topography, predation or dispersal generated the concentration
a claim that the concentration itself causes future population decline
a claim that Gamma-Poisson CV20% estimates actual Palmer observer error
ecological_interpretation: The Palmer Adélie decline has a within-island spatial-demographic architecture: breeder distributions become progressively concentrated as island populations contract, beyond the concentration expected from lower abundance and independent counting noise alone. Independent Torgersen mapping provides phenomenon-level convergence by documenting strong subcolony-footprint contraction and habitat-structured extinction, but the unresolved census-code/GIS crosswalk prevents patch-level causal attribution.
